settings.name_in_paper: Best-arm identification in linear bandits with fixed confidence
unmapped: noise is zero-mean i.i.d. and bounded in [-sigma, sigma] (hence sigma-sub-Gaussian)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\X\subseteq \Re^d$ be a finite set of arms, where $|\X| = K$ and the $\ell_2$-norm of any arm $x\in\X$ ... is upper-bounded by $L$. ... $r(x) = x^\top \theta^* + \eps$, where $\eps$ is a zero-mean i.i.d. noise bounded in $[-\sigma;\sigma]$.

symbols.beta_apx: approximation factor of the method used to compute the G-optimal allocation
symbols.log_n_term: log_n(K^2/delta) = log(c' n^2 K^2/delta) with c' = 6/pi^2

source.label: thm:g.allocation
source.quote: If the $G$-allocation strategy is implemented with a $\beta$-approximate method and the stopping condition in Eq.~\ref{eq:emp.stop.condition.2} is used, then $\Prob\bigg[ N^G \leq \frac{16c^2 d (1+\beta)\log_n(K^2/\delta)}{\Delta_{\min}^2} \wedge \Pi(\htheta_{N^G}) = x^* \bigg] \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: c^2 = 8 sigma^2 substituted. The log term depends on n itself (implicit). Holds jointly with correct identification w.p. 1-delta.

symbols.beta_apx: approximation factor of the method used to compute the XY allocation
symbols.log_n_term: log_n(K^2/delta) = log(c' n^2 K^2/delta) with c' = 6/pi^2

source.label: thm:xy.allocation
source.quote: If the $\X\Y$-allocation strategy is implemented with a $\beta$-approximate method and the stopping condition in Eq.~\ref{eq:emp.stop.condition.2} is used, then $\Prob\bigg[ N^{\X\Y} \leq \frac{32c^2 d (1+\beta)\log_n(K^2/\delta)}{\Delta_{\min}^2} \wedge \Pi(\htheta_{N^{\X\Y}}) = x^* \bigg] \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: c^2 = 8 sigma^2 substituted. Log term implicit in n.

symbols.beta_apx: approximation factor of the allocation method
symbols.M_star: minimum number of steps of static XY-allocation to discard all suboptimal directions (Eq. m.value)
symbols.N_star: oracle sample complexity c^2 H_LB log_n(K^2/delta), H_LB = min_lambda max_{y in Y*} ||y||^2_{Lambda^-1}/Delta^2(y)
symbols.log_n_term: log_n(K^2/delta) = log(c' n^2 K^2/delta) with c' = 6/pi^2

source.label: thm:xy.adaptive
source.quote: If the $\X\Y$-Adaptive allocation strategy is implemented with a $\beta$-approximate method and the stopping condition in Eq.~\ref{eq:emp.stop.condition.2} is used, then $\Prob\bigg[ N \leq \frac{(1+\beta)\max\{M^*,\frac{16}{\alpha}N^*\}}{\log(1/\alpha)} \log\Big(\frac{c\sqrt{\log_n(K^2/\delta)}}{\Delta_{\min}}\Big) \wedge \Pi(\htheta_{N}) = x^* \bigg] \geq 1-\delta.$

results.notes: c = 2 sqrt(2) sigma substituted inside the log. Lemma 2 (range of H_LB: max||y||^2/(L Delta_min^2) <= H_LB <= 4d/Delta_min^2; H_MAB <= H_LB <= 2 H_MAB for canonical basis) not recorded as it bounds a complexity measure, not an algorithm guarantee.
